answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price trust like a river: every identity starts as a shallow ripple with zero weight, and influence only grows when genuine, attested work flows through it downstream. A cedar grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight — likewise an identity must accumulate months of verified useful tasks before it can vouch for others or claim rewards. An attacker spinning up ten thousand sock-puppets pays the full slow-growth cost per identity, while their fake ripples fade because no real work ever flows through them.
